title: Lantern Ledger: commit before notifying
dek: Moving publication past the commit prevents notifications for rolled-back payments, but leaves delivery as a separate operation.
meta: Fictional change · Source and supplied in-memory probe
footer: Based on the supplied source, transaction contracts, and probe evidence.

sections.title: A callback is not a commit
sections.content:
Lantern Ledger marks a payment as paid and publishes a notification for its identifier. Originally, both awaited operations ran inside the database transaction callback. The database commits staged writes only after that callback fulfills, so publication happened before commit.

The notification is external to the transaction. Putting publish(id) inside the callback makes the database wait for it, but cannot make a rollback retract it.

sections.title: A notification could outlive a rollback
sections.content:
A failed commit could leave you with a notification for an unpaid record. The supplied probe demonstrates this: the original function publishes once, then rolls back when commit fails. Publication can also become visible before its own promise rejects, triggering a rollback after the notification escapes.

The author describes the change as making payment and notification atomic. The source supports a narrower guarantee: it orders publication after a successful commit. These operations still cannot succeed or fail as one unit.

sections.content:

That promise fulfills only after commit. A write or commit rejection therefore exits the function before publication. The next statement runs outside the callback:

{{CODE:1}}

Publication failure now leaves the payment committed. In the supplied results, rejection before visibility leaves zero notifications; rejection after visibility leaves one. Both calls report an error, so an error alone cannot tell you whether delivery occurred.

The probe models staged writes and an external counter, rather than a real database. Its assertions cover ordering and these failure outcomes; it does not simulate a process stopping.

sections.title: Safer ordering, separate delivery
sections.content: Failed transactions no longer reach publication. Delivery remains vulnerable to a process stopping between commit and publish, with no durable outbox or background retry supplied. Retrying after a visible notification can duplicate it. An idempotent markPaid does not deduplicate publication: the probe's two concurrent calls produce two notifications in both versions. This change fixes premature notification, not atomic or exactly-once delivery.
